When it reaches the space before the bracket, the optional group `(?:\s+\[(.+?)\])?` is evaluated. Since `?` is greedy, it attempts the match (1 occurrence) before skipping it (0 occurrences). The inner pattern matches `[error-code]` and `$` matches the end of the string, resulting in a successful overall match that correctly captures the error code. Skipping the optional group would require expanding the lazy `(.+?)` further, which the regex engine does not do because it already found a valid match.
